facts.fact: SNV says its GARBAL call service, run since 2015 with the Ministry of Animal Resources and ANAM, integrates satellite data with weather station and government data to advise farmers and herders.
SNV says GARBAL has over 260,000 unique users and about 2 million calls, and 1,105,000 people were mobilised.

facts.fact: Burkina Faso's national drought forecasting and early-warning process (climatology directorate, May 2023 GWP presentation) uses NDVI and VCI vegetation indices among its drought indicators, with agricultural alert thresholds by climate zone, and the country has one satellite-image reception station.

facts.fact: ANAM describes its ten-day agro-meteorological bulletin for Burkina Faso as a current product carrying NDVI and NDVI anomalies with rainfall, temperature and humidity anomalies.
ANAM publishes the bulletin every ten days, the newest listed update covering 13-19 October 2026.

facts.fact: A 2024 CIRAD journal study by Burkinabe and partner researchers tested, for the first time, NDVI and FAPAR satellite variables to estimate pasture fodder yields across Burkina Faso's climatic zones, with weak results outside the Sahel (R2 press 0.07 to 0.36).

facts.fact: Faso7 reports that the government's PPACI-BF index insurance project, run by the environment ministry's SP/CNDD, assesses seasons with automatic rain gauge data from the national meteorological agency ANAM and with satellite data.
The PPACI-BF coordinator says 4,197 people, 40 percent women, had subscribed to the index insurance by 2025, and about 1,000 farmers were paid roughly 15.3 million FCFA from 2020 to 2024.
